title: security.txt must be fetchable over HTTP
untested_rationale: check-security-txt.mjs's main() emits this id on a non-2xx HTTP status or a thrown fetch error (DNS/TLS/timeout) retrieving SECURITY_TXT_URL. No pure-function input can construct an HTTP failure -- it is inherently a network-path condition, not a body-parsing one. Covered instead by: (1) the production smoke suite's route assertions (audits.yaml B1, the same incident class recorded at audits.yaml:195 for llms-full.txt/index.md), and (2) fetchStable's retry-then-fail behavior (audits/lib/http.mjs), which is exercised by this repo's own CI running the check live against jonathanlloyd.me on every scheduled run.

spec.name: RFC 9116
spec.normative_quote: RFC 9116 specifies the content and location of security.txt; it does not define behavior for transport-layer failures when a consumer attempts to retrieve it. This id covers this repo's own operational handling of that failure mode.
spec.note: No spec clause applies -- conformance_testable is false by construction, matching rule_class: operational.
spec.verification_note: clause n/a -- rule_class: operational. normative_quote is a self-authored statement about the ABSENCE of external spec coverage for this transport/fetch/presence condition; there is no external normative clause to transcribe or verify against a source.

applicability: N/A -- this id fires on a transport failure, not on the parsed body.
